### Mean quadrat-level flowering-stem-to-recruit model 
```{r}
# Recruitment can occur from the persistent seedbank when no flowering stems
# were recorded. Candidate models therefore include intercept-only and
# disturbance-only structures.
mod_re_00 <- lm(
  re_t1_log ~ 1,
  data = df_fs2r)

mod_re_0 <- lm(
  re_t1_log ~ disturbance,
  data = df_fs2r)

mod_re_10 <- lm(
  re_t1_log ~ fs_t0_log,
  data = df_fs2r)

mod_re_1 <- lm(
  re_t1_log ~ fs_t0_log + disturbance,
  data = df_fs2r)

mod_re_20 <- lm(
  re_t1_log ~ fs_t0_log * disturbance,
  data = df_fs2r)

mods_re <- list(
  mod_re_00,
  mod_re_0,
  mod_re_10,
  mod_re_1,
  mod_re_20)

mods_re_dAICc <- bbmle::AICctab(
  mods_re,
  weights = TRUE,
  sort = FALSE)$dAICc

mods_re_sorted <- order(mods_re_dAICc)

if (length(v_mod_set_re) == 0) {
  mod_re_index_best <- mods_re_sorted[1]
} else {
  mod_re_index_best <- v_mod_set_re + 1
}

v_mod_re_index <- mod_re_index_best - 1
mod_re_best <- mods_re[[mod_re_index_best]]

summary(mod_re_best)
mods_re_dAICc
```


## Mean vital-rate plots
```{r}
make_mean_prediction <- function(data, model, disturbance_var) {
  x <- seq(
    min(data$logvol_t0, na.rm = TRUE),
    max(data$logvol_t0, na.rm = TRUE),
    length.out = 200)
  
  pred <- expand_grid(
    logvol_t0 = x,
    disturbance_value = c(0, 1)) %>%
    mutate(
      logvol_t0_2 = logvol_t0^2,
      logvol_t0_3 = logvol_t0^3,
      disturbance_plot = factor(
        disturbance_value,
        levels = c(0, 1),
        labels = c('No fire', 'Fire')))
  
  pred[[disturbance_var]] <- pred$disturbance_value
  pred$prediction <- predict(
    model,
    newdata = pred,
    type = 'response')
  
  pred
}

make_mean_plot <- function(
    data, model, response, disturbance_var, title, y_lab,
    probability = FALSE) {
  pred <- make_mean_prediction(
    data = data,
    model = model,
    disturbance_var = disturbance_var)
  
  data_plot <- data %>%
    mutate(
      disturbance_plot = factor(
        .data[[disturbance_var]],
        levels = c(0, 1),
        labels = c('No fire', 'Fire')))
  
  point_layer <- if (probability) {
    geom_jitter(
      data = data_plot,
      aes(
        x = logvol_t0,
        y = .data[[response]],
        color = disturbance_plot),
      alpha = 0.15,
      size = 0.7,
      width = 0.05,
      height = 0.05)
  } else {
    geom_point(
      data = data_plot,
      aes(
        x = logvol_t0,
        y = .data[[response]],
        color = disturbance_plot),
      alpha = 0.15,
      size = 0.7)
  }
  
  p <- ggplot() +
    point_layer +
    geom_line(
      data = pred,
      aes(
        x = logvol_t0,
        y = prediction,
        color = disturbance_plot),
      linewidth = 0.8) +
    scale_color_manual(
      values = c('No fire' = 'black', 'Fire' = 'red')) +
    theme_bw() +
    labs(
      title = title,
      subtitle = v_ggp_suffix,
      x = expression('log(volume)'[t0]),
      y = y_lab,
      color = NULL)
  
  if (probability) {
    p <- p + coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0, 1))
  }
  
  p
}
```

## Parameter extraction
```{r}
size_term_map <- c(
  b0 = '(Intercept)',
  b1 = 'logvol_t0',
  b2 = 'logvol_t0_2',
  b3 = 'logvol_t0_3',
  bd = 'disturbance')

lagged_size_term_map <- c(
  b0 = '(Intercept)',
  b1 = 'logvol_t0',
  b2 = 'logvol_t0_2',
  b3 = 'logvol_t0_3',
  bd = 'disturbance_prev')

extract_terms <- function(model, prefix, term_map) {
  coefs <- stats::coef(model)
  
  values <- vapply(term_map, function(term_i) {
    if (term_i %in% names(coefs)) {
      unname(coefs[[term_i]])
    } else {
      0
    }
  }, numeric(1))
  
  names(values) <- paste0(prefix, names(term_map))
  values
}

extract_coef <- function(model, term, default = 0) {
  coefs <- stats::coef(model)
  
  if (term %in% names(coefs)) {
    unname(coefs[[term]])
  } else {
    default
  }
}

grow_var_coef <- stats::coef(mod_gr_var)

mesh_limits <- range(
  c(
    df_gr$logvol_t0,
    df_gr$logvol_t1,
    df_recr$logvol_t0),
  na.rm = TRUE,
  finite = TRUE)
mesh_limits <- c(mesh_limits[1] - 0.1, mesh_limits[2] + 0.1)

pars_mean <- as.list(c(
  extract_terms(mod_su_best, 'surv_', size_term_map),
  extract_terms(mod_gr_best, 'grow_', size_term_map),
  extract_terms(mod_fl_best, 'fl_', lagged_size_term_map),
  extract_terms(mod_fl_n_best, 'fln_', lagged_size_term_map),
  re_b0 = extract_coef(
    mod_re_best,
    '(Intercept)'),
  re_b1 = extract_coef(
    mod_re_best,
    'fs_t0_log'),
  re_bd = extract_coef(
    mod_re_best,
    'disturbance'),
  re_bf = extract_coef(
    mod_re_best,
    'fs_t0_log:disturbance'),
  re_sigma = stats::sigma(mod_re_best),
  recr_mean = rc_sz$mean,
  recr_sd = rc_sz$sd,
  grow_var_a = unname(grow_var_coef[['a']]),
  grow_var_b = unname(grow_var_coef[['b']]),
  fs_ref = mean(df_fs2r$fs_t0, na.rm = TRUE),
  L = mesh_limits[1],
  U = mesh_limits[2],
  mat_siz = 200,
  mod_su_index = v_mod_su_index,
  mod_gr_index = v_mod_gr_index,
  mod_fl_index = v_mod_fl_index,
  mod_fl_n_index = v_mod_fl_n_index,
  mod_re_index = v_mod_re_index))

pars_mean_table <- tibble(
  parameter = names(pars_mean),
  value = as.numeric(unlist(pars_mean)))

pars_mean_table
```

## IPM functions 
The fitted model coefficients are translated into continuous demographic
functions for survival, growth, flowering, flowering-stem production, and
recruitment. Importantly, the distinction between current and previous
disturbance is retained: survival and growth depend on disturbance, while
flowering and flowering-stem production depend on disturbance_prev.
Recruitment combines flowering-stem production at $t$ with the effect of
current disturbance on recruitment from $t$ to $t+1$.
```{r}
get_par <- function(pars, par_name, default = 0) {
  if (!is.null(pars[[par_name]])) {
    pars[[par_name]]
  } else {
    default
  }
}

vital_lp <- function(x, pars, prefix, disturbance = 0) {
  get_par(pars, paste0(prefix, 'b0')) +
    get_par(pars, paste0(prefix, 'b1')) * x +
    get_par(pars, paste0(prefix, 'b2')) * x^2 +
    get_par(pars, paste0(prefix, 'b3')) * x^3 +
    get_par(pars, paste0(prefix, 'bd')) * disturbance
}


# Survival ---------------------------------------------------------------------
sx <- function(x, pars, disturbance = 0) {
  plogis(vital_lp(
    x = x,
    pars = pars,
    prefix = 'surv_',
    disturbance = disturbance))
}


# Growth -----------------------------------------------------------------------
grow_mu <- function(x, pars, disturbance = 0) {
  vital_lp(
    x = x,
    pars = pars,
    prefix = 'grow_',
    disturbance = disturbance)
}

grow_sd <- function(mean_value, pars) {
  variance <- get_par(pars, 'grow_var_a') *
    exp(get_par(pars, 'grow_var_b') * mean_value)
  
  sqrt(pmax(variance, .Machine$double.eps))
}

gxy <- function(x, y, pars, disturbance = 0) {
  mean_value <- grow_mu(
    x = x,
    pars = pars,
    disturbance = disturbance)
  
  sd_value <- grow_sd(
    mean_value = mean_value,
    pars = pars)
  
  dnorm(y, mean = mean_value, sd = sd_value)
}


# Flowering probability --------------------------------------------------------
fl_x <- function(x, pars, disturbance_prev = 0) {
  plogis(vital_lp(
    x = x,
    pars = pars,
    prefix = 'fl_',
    disturbance = disturbance_prev))
}


# Flowering-stem number conditional on flowering ------------------------------
fln_x <- function(x, pars, disturbance_prev = 0) {
  exp(vital_lp(
    x = x,
    pars = pars,
    prefix = 'fln_',
    disturbance = disturbance_prev))
}


# Expected flowering stems per individual ------------------------------------
fs_x <- function(x, pars, disturbance_prev = 0) {
  fl_x(
    x = x,
    pars = pars,
    disturbance_prev = disturbance_prev) *
    fln_x(
      x = x,
      pars = pars,
      disturbance_prev = disturbance_prev)
}


# Flowering-stem-to-recruit conversion ----------------------------------------
predict_recruits_from_stems <- function(
    flowering_stems, pars, disturbance = 0) {
  stems_nonnegative <- pmax(flowering_stems, 0)
  
  slope <- get_par(pars, 're_b1') +
    get_par(pars, 're_bf') * disturbance
  
  eta <- get_par(pars, 're_b0') +
    get_par(pars, 're_bd') * disturbance +
    slope * log1p(stems_nonnegative)
  
  recruits <- expm1(
    eta + 0.5 * get_par(pars, 're_sigma')^2)
  
  pmax(recruits, 0)
}

recruits_per_stem <- function(pars, disturbance = 0) {
  fs_ref <- get_par(pars, 'fs_ref', 0)
  
  if (!is.finite(fs_ref) || fs_ref <= 0) {
    return(0)
  }
  
  predict_recruits_from_stems(
    flowering_stems = fs_ref,
    pars = pars,
    disturbance = disturbance) / fs_ref
}

rx <- function(
    x, pars, disturbance = 0, disturbance_prev = 0) {
  fs_x(
    x = x,
    pars = pars,
    disturbance_prev = disturbance_prev) *
    recruits_per_stem(
      pars = pars,
      disturbance = disturbance)
}


# Recruit size distribution ----------------------------------------------------
recr_y <- function(y, pars) {
  dnorm(
    y,
    mean = get_par(pars, 'recr_mean'),
    sd = get_par(pars, 'recr_sd'))
}


# Fertility matrix -------------------------------------------------------------
fy <- function(
    y, x, pars, h, disturbance = 0, disturbance_prev = 0) {
  Pvec <- recr_y(y, pars)
  recruit_mass <- sum(Pvec * h)
  
  if (!is.finite(recruit_mass) || recruit_mass <= 0) {
    stop('Recruit size distribution has no mass inside the mesh')
  }
  
  Pvec <- Pvec / recruit_mass
  
  Rvec <- rx(
    x = x,
    pars = pars,
    disturbance = disturbance,
    disturbance_prev = disturbance_prev)
  
  outer(Pvec, Rvec) * h
}
```

## Kernel
For a specified combination of current and previous disturbance, the
demographic functions are combined into a size-structured projection kernel.
The survival-growth component describes the contribution of individuals at
size $x$ at time $t$ to surviving individuals of size $y$ at $t+1$, while the
fecundity component describes the contribution of those individuals to new
recruits. Because flowering depends on previous disturbance whereas survival,
growth, and recruitment depend on current disturbance, the resulting kernel is
conditional on both disturbance states.
```{r}
kernel <- function(
    pars, disturbance = 0, disturbance_prev = 0) {
  n <- as.integer(pars$mat_siz)
  L <- pars$L
  U <- pars$U
  h <- (U - L) / n
  
  b <- L + c(0:n) * h
  y <- 0.5 * (b[1:n] + b[2:(n + 1)])
  
  Fmat <- fy(
    y = y,
    x = y,
    pars = pars,
    h = h,
    disturbance = disturbance,
    disturbance_prev = disturbance_prev)
  
  Smat <- sx(
    x = y,
    pars = pars,
    disturbance = disturbance)
  
  Gmat <- matrix(0, n, n)
  Gmat[] <- t(
    outer(
      y,
      y,
      Vectorize(function(x, y) {
        gxy(
          x = x,
          y = y,
          pars = pars,
          disturbance = disturbance)
      }))) * h
  
  Tmat <- matrix(0, n, n)
  
  for (i in 1:(n / 2)) {
    Gmat[1, i] <- Gmat[1, i] + 1 - sum(Gmat[, i])
    Tmat[, i] <- Gmat[, i] * Smat[i]
  }
  
  for (i in (n / 2 + 1):n) {
    Gmat[n, i] <- Gmat[n, i] + 1 - sum(Gmat[, i])
    Tmat[, i] <- Gmat[, i] * Smat[i]
  }
  
  k_yx <- Fmat + Tmat
  
  list(
    k_yx = k_yx,
    Fmat = Fmat,
    Tmat = Tmat,
    Gmat = Gmat,
    Smat = Smat,
    meshpts = y,
    h = h)
}

lambda_ipm <- function(
    pars, disturbance = 0, disturbance_prev = 0) {
  K <- kernel(
    pars = pars,
    disturbance = disturbance,
    disturbance_prev = disturbance_prev)$k_yx
  
  Re(eigen(K, only.values = TRUE)$values[1])
}
```



## Mean observed size distribution
A mean observed population size distribution is used as the initial
size-structured population vector. Annual size-frequency distributions are
first constructed from the observed plants and then averaged across years.
Recruits without a usable size measurement are distributed according to the
fitted recruit-size distribution.
```{r}
# The vector is the arithmetic mean of annual size-frequency vectors. Unsized
# recruits are distributed over the fitted recruit-size distribution.
make_initial_n_mean <- function(pars, df_init = df) {
  n <- as.integer(pars$mat_siz)
  L <- pars$L
  U <- pars$U
  h <- (U - L) / n
  breaks <- seq(L, U, length.out = n + 1)
  b <- L + c(0:n) * h
  y <- 0.5 * (b[1:n] + b[2:(n + 1)])
  
  recruit_density <- recr_y(y, pars)
  recruit_density <- recruit_density / sum(recruit_density * h)
  
  years_i <- df_init %>%
    filter(!is.na(year)) %>%
    distinct(year) %>%
    arrange(year) %>%
    pull(year)
  
  counts_by_year <- purrr::map(years_i, function(year_i) {
    df_i <- df_init %>%
      filter(year == year_i)
    
    x <- df_i %>%
      filter(is.finite(logvol_t0)) %>%
      pull(logvol_t0)
    
    size_counts <- hist(
      pmin(pmax(x, L), U),
      breaks = breaks,
      plot = FALSE,
      include.lowest = TRUE)$counts
    
    n_unsized_recruits <- df_i %>%
      summarise(
        n = sum(
          !is.finite(logvol_t0) & recruits == 1,
          na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
      pull(n)
    
    size_counts + n_unsized_recruits * recruit_density * h
  })
  
  mean_counts <- Reduce(`+`, counts_by_year) / length(counts_by_year)
  mean_counts / h
}


# Quadrat-level flowering-stem reference --------------------------------------
# The flowering-stem-to-recruit model is fitted to quadrat-year totals.
# Its flowering-stem reference must therefore also be on the quadrat scale.
df_fs2r_previous_fire <- df_fs2r %>%

    fs_ref = mean(fs_t0),

    .groups = "drop")

get_stem_reference <- function(disturbance_prev_i) {

    filter(
      disturbance_prev ==

}

mean_stems_no_previous_fire <- get_stem_reference(0)
mean_stems_previous_fire <- get_stem_reference(1)

df_stem_reference
```

## Disturbance history
```{r}
# Each sampled quadrat-year receives equal weight. Current disturbance refers
# to the interval t -> t + 1 and previous disturbance to t - 1 -> t.
df_disturbance_regime <- df %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(quad),
    !is.na(year),
    !is.na(disturbance),
    !is.na(disturbance_prev)) %>%
  distinct(
    quad,
    year,
    disturbance,
    disturbance_prev) %>%
  count(
    disturbance,
    disturbance_prev,
    name = 'n_quadrat_years') %>%
  complete(
    disturbance = c(0, 1),
    disturbance_prev = c(0, 1),
    fill = list(n_quadrat_years = 0)) %>%
  arrange(
    disturbance_prev,
    disturbance)

df_disturbance_regime
```

## Disturbance transition probabilities
The environmental historical model requires not only the frequency of fire,
but also information on how fire states follow one another through time.
Disturbance is therefore represented by two states: disturbance_prev,
describing fire during $t-1$ to $t$, and disturbance, describing fire during
$t$ to $t+1$. Together they define four possible disturbance histories: no
fire in either interval, current fire only, previous fire only, or fire in
both intervals.

The observed quadrat-year histories are used to estimate conditional
disturbance-transition probabilities,

$$
P(D_t \mid D_{t-1}),
$$

which determine the probability of entering each current disturbance state
given the disturbance state during the preceding interval.

Four demographic kernels are consequently required,

$$
\mathbf{K}{00},\quad
\mathbf{K}{01},\quad
\mathbf{K}{10},\quad
\mathbf{K}{11},
$$

where the first subscript denotes current disturbance and the second denotes
previous disturbance. These kernels are combined with the conditional
disturbance-transition probabilities to form the environmental historical
megamatrix,

$$
\mathbf{K}{\mathrm{env}} =
\begin{pmatrix}
p{0|0}\mathbf{K}{00} &
p{0|1}\mathbf{K}{01} \
p{1|0}\mathbf{K}{10} &
p{1|1}\mathbf{K}_{11}
\end{pmatrix}.
$$

With 200 size classes for each previous-disturbance state, the resulting
historical projection matrix has dimensions $400 \times 400$.

$$
P(D_t \mid D_{t-1}).
$$

These probabilities describe how likely each current disturbance state is
given the disturbance state experienced during the preceding interval.

```{r}
# Environmental transitions are conditional probabilities:
# P(disturbance_t | disturbance_t-1).
df_disturbance_transition <- df_disturbance_regime %>%
  group_by(disturbance_prev) %>%
  mutate(
    p_transition = n_quadrat_years /
      sum(n_quadrat_years)) %>%
  ungroup()

df_disturbance_transition

get_transition_probability <- function(
    disturbance_i, disturbance_prev_i) {
  df_disturbance_transition %>%
    filter(
      disturbance == disturbance_i,
      disturbance_prev == disturbance_prev_i) %>%
    pull(p_transition)
}

p_0_given_0 <- get_transition_probability(0, 0)
p_1_given_0 <- get_transition_probability(1, 0)
p_0_given_1 <- get_transition_probability(0, 1)
p_1_given_1 <- get_transition_probability(1, 1)


# Previous-disturbance probabilities ------------------------------------------
# These probabilities are used only to divide the initial observed population
# between the two environmental-history states.
df_previous_disturbance <- df_disturbance_regime %>%
  group_by(disturbance_prev) %>%
  summarise(
    n_quadrat_years = sum(n_quadrat_years),
    .groups = 'drop') %>%
  mutate(
    p_previous = n_quadrat_years /
      sum(n_quadrat_years))

df_previous_disturbance

p_prev_0 <- df_previous_disturbance %>%
  filter(disturbance_prev == 0) %>%
  pull(p_previous)

p_prev_1 <- df_previous_disturbance %>%
  filter(disturbance_prev == 1) %>%
  pull(p_previous)


# Parameters for previous-disturbance states ----------------------------------
# Flowering and flowering-stem production depend on disturbance in the
# preceding interval, so the flowering-stem reference also follows that state.
pars_prev_0 <- pars_mean
pars_prev_0$fs_ref <- mean_stems_no_previous_fire

pars_prev_1 <- pars_mean
pars_prev_1$fs_ref <- mean_stems_previous_fire
```


## State-specific demographic kernels 
Because the vital rates depend on different disturbance intervals, a separate
demographic kernel is constructed for each combination of previous and current
disturbance. The first index denotes disturbance during the current transition
from $t$ to $t+1$, while the second denotes disturbance during the preceding
transition from $t-1$ to $t$.

Thus, the four kernels are

$$
\mathbf{K}{00},\quad
\mathbf{K}{01},\quad
\mathbf{K}{10},\quad
\mathbf{K}{11},
$$

where, for example, $\mathbf{K}_{10}$ represents demographic transitions under
current fire following an unburned previous interval.

```{r}
# First digit  = current disturbance, t -> t + 1.
# Second digit = previous disturbance, t - 1 -> t.
K_00 <- kernel(
  pars = pars_prev_0,
  disturbance = 0,
  disturbance_prev = 0)$k_yx

K_01 <- kernel(
  pars = pars_prev_1,
  disturbance = 0,
  disturbance_prev = 1)$k_yx

K_10 <- kernel(
  pars = pars_prev_0,
  disturbance = 1,
  disturbance_prev = 0)$k_yx

K_11 <- kernel(
  pars = pars_prev_1,
  disturbance = 1,
  disturbance_prev = 1)$k_yx


# Environmental historical megamatrix ----------------------------------------
# Columns represent disturbance during t - 1 -> t.
# Rows represent disturbance during t -> t + 1.
K_env_hist <- rbind(
  cbind(
    p_0_given_0 * K_00,
    p_0_given_1 * K_01),
  cbind(
    p_1_given_0 * K_10,
    p_1_given_1 * K_11))


# Environmental historical asymptotic lambda ----------------------------------
lambda_env_hist <- Re(
  eigen(
    K_env_hist,
    only.values = TRUE)$values[1])

lambda_env_hist
```


## Asymptotic and projected lambda 
Population growth is evaluated both for the four individual
disturbance-history kernels and for the complete environmental historical
model. The asymptotic growth rate is obtained from the dominant eigenvalue of
the respective projection matrix, whereas the projected growth rate describes
the change in abundance during a single projection from the observed mean size
distribution.

For the environmental historical model, the initial 200-element size
distribution is divided between the two previous-disturbance states according
to their observed frequencies. The two components therefore represent
different parts of the same population and together retain the original total
abundance.

```{r}
# Mean observed size distribution used for the four fixed environmental states.
n_obs <- make_initial_n_mean(pars_mean)

n <- as.integer(pars_mean$mat_siz)
h <- (pars_mean$U - pars_mean$L) / n

# For the environmental historical IPM, the observed population is divided
# between the two previous-disturbance states. The two blocks are mutually
# exclusive parts of the same population and therefore must not be duplicated.
n_env_initial <- c(
  p_prev_0 * n_obs,
  p_prev_1 * n_obs)


# General projection function -------------------------------------------------
project_kernel <- function(K, n_initial, h, label) {
  n_initial_total <- sum(n_initial) * h
  
  n_proj <- as.numeric(K %*% n_initial)
  n_projected <- sum(n_proj) * h
  
  tibble(
    lambda_type = label,
    asym_lambda = Re(eigen(K, only.values = TRUE)$values[1]),
    proj_lambda = n_projected / n_initial_total,
    n_initial = n_initial_total,
    n_projected = n_projected)
}


# Fixed disturbance-state lambdas ---------------------------------------------
make_state_lambda <- function(
    K, label, disturbance, disturbance_prev) {
  project_kernel(
    K = K,
    n_initial = n_obs,
    h = h,
    label = label) %>%
    mutate(
      disturbance = disturbance,
      disturbance_prev = disturbance_prev)
}

df_lambda_states <- bind_rows(
  make_state_lambda(
    K = K_00,
    label = 'Undisturbed',
    disturbance = 0,
    disturbance_prev = 0),
  make_state_lambda(
    K = K_10,
    label = 'Current-year fire',
    disturbance = 1,
    disturbance_prev = 0),
  make_state_lambda(
    K = K_01,
    label = 'Previous-year fire',
    disturbance = 0,
    disturbance_prev = 1),
  make_state_lambda(
    K = K_11,
    label = 'Fire in both years',
    disturbance = 1,
    disturbance_prev = 1))


# Environmental historical regime --------------------------------------------
df_lambda_env_hist <- project_kernel(
  K = K_env_hist,
  n_initial = n_env_initial,
  h = h,
  label = 'Environmental historical regime') %>%
  mutate(
    disturbance = NA_real_,
    disturbance_prev = NA_real_)


# Combined lambda table --------------------------------------------------------
df_lambda_env <- bind_rows(
  df_lambda_states,
  df_lambda_env_hist)

df_lambda_env
```


## Observed annual abundance change
Observed population growth is calculated independently from the IPM using
annual changes in abundance. Only quadrats represented in both consecutive
years are retained so that abundance at $t$ and $t+1$ refers to the same set
of sampling units. Annual population growth is then calculated as

$$
\lambda_t = \frac{N_{t+1}}{N_t}.
$$

Because population growth is multiplicative through time, the geometric mean
of annual $\lambda_t$ values is used as the summary measure of observed
population growth across the study period.

```{r}
# Counts include sized plants and recruits without a usable size measurement.
# Only quadrats with individual records in both consecutive years are retained.
df_counts_quad_year <- df %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(site),
    !is.na(quad),
    !is.na(year)) %>%
  group_by(site, quad, year) %>%
  summarise(
    n_sized = sum(
      is.finite(logvol_t0),
      na.rm = TRUE),
    n_unsized_recruits = sum(
      !is.finite(logvol_t0) & recruits == 1,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    n_t0 = n_sized + n_unsized_recruits,
    .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(site, quad, year) %>%
  group_by(site, quad) %>%
  mutate(
    year_t1 = lead(year),
    n_t1 = lead(n_t0),
    year_gap = year_t1 - year) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(year_gap == 1)

df_obs_growth_year <- df_counts_quad_year %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(
    n_t0 = sum(n_t0),
    n_t1 = sum(n_t1),
    n_quadrats = n(),
    n_sites = n_distinct(site),
    obs_lambda = n_t1 / n_t0,
    .groups = "drop") %>%
  filter(n_t0 > 0)

df_obs_growth_year


df_obs_growth_summary <- df_obs_growth_year %>%
  summarise(
    n_transitions = n(),
    lambda_arithmetic = mean(obs_lambda, na.rm = TRUE),
    lambda_geometric = exp(mean(log(obs_lambda), na.rm = TRUE)),
    lambda_median = median(obs_lambda, na.rm = TRUE),
    lambda_min = min(obs_lambda, na.rm = TRUE),
    lambda_max = max(obs_lambda, na.rm = TRUE))

df_obs_growth_summary
```


## Observed and modeled population growth through time
Model-based population growth is compared with population change observed
directly in the monitoring data. Annual abundance changes are calculated from
quadrats sampled in both consecutive years so that abundance at $t$ and
$t+1$ refers to the same sampling units.

For each annual transition, observed population growth is calculated as

$$
\lambda_t =
\frac{N_{t+1}}{N_t}.
$$

Because population growth compounds multiplicatively through time, the
geometric mean of the annual growth rates is used to describe mean observed
population growth across the monitoring period.

# Yearly historical kuss projection model {#yr-ipm-hist-kuss}
## Introduction

This analysis develops a **year-specific historical integral projection model
(IPM)** for *Polygala lewtonii* at Archbold. The model combines annual variation
in demographic rates with the delayed contribution of reproduction to
recruitment.

Survival, growth, flowering, flowering-stem production, and recruitment are
first modeled separately. Year-specific demographic variation is introduced
through the year effects from the fitted mixed models. This means that each
annual IPM uses the demographic conditions estimated for that particular year,
rather than applying one mean set of vital-rate parameters to the full time
series.

Disturbance is incorporated as a single common fire state within the IPM.
Survival, growth, flowering, flowering-stem production, and recruitment are
therefore evaluated under either

- no disturbance (`disturbance = 0`), or
- disturbance (`disturbance = 1`).

This deliberately places disturbance on the same level for all demographic
processes inside the IPM. The underlying flowering and flower-number models are
still fitted using previous-year disturbance, as in the original demographic
models, but their disturbance coefficients are applied to the common
disturbance state when the IPM is constructed.

The historical structure is needed because flowering in year \(t\) contributes
to recruitment in year \(t+1\). The population state therefore contains both
the current and previous size distributions,

\[
\mathbf{n}^{H}_t =
\begin{pmatrix}
\mathbf{n}_t \\
\mathbf{n}_{t-1}
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

The corresponding historical kernel is

\[
\mathbf{K}^{H}_t =
\begin{pmatrix}
\mathbf{T}_t & \mathbf{F}_t \\
\mathbf{I}   & \mathbf{0}
\end{pmatrix},
\]

where \(\mathbf{T}_t\) contains survival and growth, \(\mathbf{F}_t\) contains
fertility, \(\mathbf{I}\) transfers the current population into the lagged
state, and \(\mathbf{0}\) prevents the lagged state from persisting beyond one
year. Projection therefore gives

\[
\begin{pmatrix}
\mathbf{n}_{t+1} \\
\mathbf{n}_t
\end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix}
\mathbf{T}_t & \mathbf{F}_t \\
\mathbf{I}   & \mathbf{0}
\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}
\mathbf{n}_t \\
\mathbf{n}_{t-1}
\end{pmatrix}.
\]

For the **year-specific model**, a separate historical kernel is constructed
for each year using that year's demographic parameters. For every year, two
asymptotic scenarios are evaluated: one assuming no fire and one assuming
fire. The dominant eigenvalue of the corresponding historical kernel gives the
year-specific asymptotic population growth rate under that disturbance state.

The yearly model is also used for one-step projections of the observed
population. For each quadrat-year transition, the observed size distribution
in year \(t\) is combined with the observed size distribution from year
\(t-1\). The historical kernel for year \(t\), using the observed disturbance
state of that quadrat, is then applied once to obtain the predicted population
in year \(t+1\).

The projected population growth rate is calculated as

\[
\lambda_{\mathrm{proj},t}
=
\frac{N_{\mathrm{projected},t+1}}
     {N_{\mathrm{observed},t}}.
\]

This differs from the asymptotic growth rate. The projected lambda depends on
the actual observed population structure in years \(t\) and \(t-1\), whereas
the asymptotic lambda is determined by the dominant eigenvalue of the annual
historical kernel and represents the long-term growth rate that would result
if the demographic conditions and disturbance state of that year were held
constant.

Observed population growth from \(t\) to \(t+1\) is then compared with both the
projected and asymptotic growth rates. This allows the year-specific model to
be evaluated against the realized annual population dynamics while retaining
the historical lag between flowering and recruitment.



## Working dataset
```{r}
df <- read.csv(
  file.path(
    dir_data,
    paste0('ab_', v_sp_abb, '_df_workdata_260519.csv'))) %>%
  mutate(
    disturbance = as.numeric(dist_transition),
    disturbance_prev = as.numeric(disturbance_prev),
    year = as.integer(year),
    site = factor(site)) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(year),
    !(year %in% v_years_re))
```

### Controls
```{r}
ctrl_glmer <- glmerControl(
  optimizer = 'bobyqa',
  optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5))

ctrl_lmer <- lmerControl(
  optimizer = 'bobyqa',
  optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5))
```

## Vital rates
### Survival
```{r}
df_su <- df %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(survives),
    size_t0 != 0,
    is.finite(logvol_t0),
    is.finite(logvol_t0_2),
    is.finite(logvol_t0_3),
    !is.na(disturbance)) %>%
  mutate(
    year = factor(year),
    disturbance = factor(disturbance, levels = c(0, 1))) %>%
  dplyr::select(
    id, site, year, size_t0, survives, size_t1,
    logsize_t0, logsize_t1, logsize_t0_2, logsize_t0_3,
    volume_t0, volume_t1, logvol_t0, logvol_t1,
    logvol_t0_2, logvol_t0_3,
    disturbance, stage)


# Survival model ---------------------------------------------------------------
mod_su_0 <- glmer(
  survives ~ disturbance + (1 | year),
  data = df_su, family = binomial, control = ctrl_glmer)
mod_su_10 <- glmer(
  survives ~ logvol_t0 + (1 | year),
  data = df_su, family = binomial, control = ctrl_glmer)
mod_su_11 <- glmer(
  survives ~ logvol_t0 + disturbance + (1 | year),
  data = df_su, family = binomial, control = ctrl_glmer)
mod_su_20 <- glmer(
  survives ~ logvol_t0 + logvol_t0_2 + (1 | year),
  data = df_su, family = binomial, control = ctrl_glmer)
mod_su_21 <- glmer(
  survives ~ logvol_t0 + logvol_t0_2 + disturbance + (1 | year),
  data = df_su, family = binomial, control = ctrl_glmer)
mod_su_30 <- glmer(
  survives ~ logvol_t0 + logvol_t0_2 + logvol_t0_3 +
    (1 | year),
  data = df_su, family = binomial, control = ctrl_glmer)
mod_su_31 <- glmer(
  survives ~ logvol_t0 + logvol_t0_2 + logvol_t0_3 + disturbance +
    (1 | year),
  data = df_su, family = binomial, control = ctrl_glmer)


mods_su <- list(
  mod_su_0, mod_su_10, mod_su_11, 
  mod_su_20, mod_su_21, mod_su_30, mod_su_31)
mods_su_dAIC <- bbmle::AICctab(mods_su, weights = TRUE, sort = FALSE)$dAIC
mods_su_sorted <- order(mods_su_dAIC)

if (length(v_mod_set_su) == 0) {
  mod_su_index_bestfit <- mods_su_sorted[1]
  v_mod_su_index <- mod_su_index_bestfit - 1
} else {
  mod_su_index_bestfit <- v_mod_set_su + 1
  v_mod_su_index <- v_mod_set_su
}

mod_su_best <- mods_su[[mod_su_index_bestfit]]
mod_su_ranef <- coef(mod_su_best)$year

mod_su_best
summary(mod_su_best)
mods_su_dAIC

```


```{r}
# Survival plots by year -------------------------------------------------------
make_su_year_plot <- function(year_i) {
  df_i <- df_su %>% filter(year == year_i)
  
  x <- seq(
    min(df_i$logvol_t0, na.rm = TRUE),
    max(df_i$logvol_t0, na.rm = TRUE), length.out = 100)
  
  pred_i <- tidyr::expand_grid(
    logvol_t0 = x,
    disturbance = levels(df_su$disturbance)) %>%
    mutate(
      logvol_t0_2 = logvol_t0^2,
      logvol_t0_3 = logvol_t0^3,
      disturbance = factor(
        disturbance, levels = levels(df_su$disturbance)),
      year = factor(year_i, levels = levels(df_su$year)))
  
  pred_i$survives <- predict(
    mod_su_best, newdata = pred_i,
    type = "response", re.form = NULL)
  
  pts_i <- df_i %>%
    mutate(bin = cut(logvol_t0, breaks = 8)) %>%
    group_by(bin, disturbance) %>%
    summarise(
      logvol_t0 = mean(logvol_t0, na.rm = TRUE),
      survives = mean(survives, na.rm = TRUE),
      n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
    filter(!is.na(logvol_t0), n > 0)
  
  ggplot() +
    geom_point(
      data = pts_i,
      aes(logvol_t0, survives, color = disturbance), size = 1.1) +
    geom_line(
      data = pred_i,
      aes(logvol_t0, survives, color = disturbance,
          linetype = disturbance),
      linewidth = 0.7) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c("0" = "black", "1" = "red")) +
    labs(
      title = year_i,
      x = expression("log(volume)"[t0]),
      y = expression("Survival probability"[t1])) +
    ylim(0, 1) +
    theme_bw() +
    theme(text = element_text(size = 5), legend.position = "none")
}

su_yrs <- lapply(levels(df_su$year), make_su_year_plot)
fig_su_years <- wrap_plots(su_yrs) +
  plot_layout(ncol = 4) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = 'Survival - year specific',
    subtitle = v_ggp_suffix,
    theme = theme(
      plot.title = element_text(size = 13, face = 'bold'),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9)))

fig_su_years
```

### Flowering probability
```{r}
# Flower data ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Recruits should theoretically be excluded from flowering probability and flower-number models.
# That exclusion is not supported by the data, because 35 recruits did flower, 
# including several fairly large individuals and some stage-3 plants.
df_fl <- df %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(flower),
    is.finite(logvol_t0),
    is.finite(logvol_t0_2),
    is.finite(logvol_t0_3),

    year = factor(year),

    logvol_t0_2, logvol_t0_3,

# Flower model -----------------------------------------------------------------
```

### Flwoers to recuit transition
```{r}
# Flowering stems to recruits --------------------------------------------------
# Total flowering stems in quadrat q during year t predict recruits in the
# same quadrat during year t + 1. Current fire is retained at the quadrat level.
df_quad_year_sampled <- df %>%
  distinct(
    site,
    quad,
    year)

df_fs2r <- df %>%
  group_by(
    site,
    quad,
    year) %>%
  summarise(
    fs_t0 = sum(
      fl_nr,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    disturbance = first(
      disturbance[!is.na(disturbance)],
      default = NA_real_),
    .groups = 'drop') %>%
  mutate(
    year_t1 = year + 1) %>%
  semi_join(
    df_quad_year_sampled %>%
      transmute(
        site,
        quad,
        year_t1 = year),
    by = c(
      'site',
      'quad',
      'year_t1')) %>%
  left_join(
    df %>%
      filter(recruits == 1) %>%
      count(
        site,
        quad,
        year,
        name = 're_t1'),
    by = c(
      'site',
      'quad',
      'year_t1' = 'year')) %>%
  mutate(
    re_t1 = replace_na(re_t1, 0L),
    fs_t0_log = log1p(fs_t0),
    re_t1_log = log1p(re_t1)) %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(year),
    !is.na(year_t1),
    !is.na(disturbance),
    !(year %in% v_years_re),
    !(year_t1 %in% v_years_re)) %>%
  mutate(
    site = factor(site),
    year_t0 = factor(year),
    year_t1 = factor(year_t1),
    disturbance_t0 = factor(
      disturbance,
      levels = c(0, 1)))

# Keep the old mean-script recruitment plot as a quick check.
fig_fs2r_raw <- ggplot(
  df_fs2r,
  aes(x = fs_t0, y = re_t1, color = disturbance_t0)) +
  geom_jitter(height = 0.2, width = 0.5, alpha = 0.4) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c('0' = 'black', '1' = 'red')) +
  theme_bw() +
  labs(
    title = 'Recruits t1 by flowering stems t0',
    subtitle = v_ggp_suffix,
    x = 'Total flowering stems in quadrat in year t',
    y = 'Number of recruits in quadrat in year t + 1',
    color = 'Fire')
```

## Parameter extraction
```{r}
# Parameter extraction helpers -------------------------------------------------
empty_coef_df <- function() {
  data.frame(coefficient = character(), value = numeric())
}

is_mixed_model <- function(model) {
  inherits(model, 'merMod')
}

get_fixef_safe <- function(model) {
  if (is_mixed_model(model)) {
    fixef(model)
  } else {
    coef(model)
  }
}

get_group_coef_safe <- function(model, group_var) {
  if (!is_mixed_model(model)) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  coef_list <- coef(model)
  if (!(group_var %in% names(coef_list))) {
    return(NULL)
  }
  coef_list[[group_var]]
}

find_model_term <- function(model_terms, aliases) {
  aliases <- unlist(aliases)
  for (alias in aliases) {
    if (grepl('^regex:', alias)) {
      pattern <- sub('^regex:', '', alias)
      hit <- grep(pattern, model_terms, value = TRUE)
    } else {
      hit <- model_terms[model_terms == alias]
    }
    if (length(hit) > 0) {
      return(hit[1])
    }
  }
  NA_character_
}

bind_coef_rows <- function(x) {
  x <- x[!vapply(x, is.null, logical(1))]
  if (length(x) == 0) {
    return(empty_coef_df())
  }
  out <- do.call(rbind, x)
  rownames(out) <- NULL
  out
}

check_duplicate_coefficients <- function(x, object_name = 'parameter table') {
  dup <- x$coefficient[duplicated(x$coefficient)]
  if (length(dup) > 0) {
    stop(
      object_name,
      ' contains duplicated coefficient names: ',
      paste(unique(dup), collapse = ', '))
  }
  invisible(TRUE)
}

coef_df_to_list <- function(x) {
  if (nrow(x) == 0) {
    return(list())
  }
  check_duplicate_coefficients(x)
  x %>%
    mutate(coefficient = as.character(coefficient)) %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = coefficient, values_from = value) %>%
    as.list()
}

extract_fixed_pars <- function(model, term_map, fill_missing = TRUE) {
  model_coefs <- get_fixef_safe(model)
  model_terms <- names(model_coefs)
  out <- lapply(names(term_map), function(coef_name) {
    model_term <- find_model_term(model_terms, term_map[[coef_name]])
    if (is.na(model_term)) {
      if (fill_missing) {
        value <- 0
      } else {
        return(NULL)
      }
    } else {
      value <- unname(model_coefs[model_term])
    }
    data.frame(coefficient = coef_name, value = value)
  })
  bind_coef_rows(out)
}

extract_group_pars <- function(model, group_var, term_map, fill_missing = TRUE) {
  coef_matrix <- get_group_coef_safe(model, group_var)
  if (is.null(coef_matrix)) {
    return(empty_coef_df())
  }
  model_terms <- colnames(coef_matrix)
  out <- lapply(names(term_map), function(coef_prefix) {
    model_term <- find_model_term(model_terms, term_map[[coef_prefix]])
    if (is.na(model_term)) {
      if (fill_missing) {
        value <- rep(0, nrow(coef_matrix))
      } else {
        return(NULL)
      }
    } else {
      value <- coef_matrix[, model_term]
    }
    data.frame(
      coefficient = paste0(coef_prefix, '_', rownames(coef_matrix)),
      value = value)
  })
  bind_coef_rows(out)
}

extract_re_ranef_devs <- function(model, group_var, group_label) {
  if (!inherits(model, 'merMod')) {
    return(empty_coef_df())
  }
  ranef_list <- ranef(model)
  if (!(group_var %in% names(ranef_list))) {
    return(empty_coef_df())
  }
  ranef_matrix <- ranef_list[[group_var]]
  out <- list()
  if ('(Intercept)' %in% colnames(ranef_matrix)) {
    out[['intercept']] <- data.frame(
      coefficient = paste0('re_u0_', group_label, '_',
                           rownames(ranef_matrix)),
      value = ranef_matrix[, '(Intercept)'])
  }
  if ('fs_t0_log' %in% colnames(ranef_matrix)) {
    out[['slope']] <- data.frame(
      coefficient = paste0('re_u1_', group_label, '_',
                           rownames(ranef_matrix)),
      value = ranef_matrix[, 'fs_t0_log'])
  }
  bind_coef_rows(out)
}
```

### Term maps 
```{r}
size_term_map <- list(
  b0 = c('(Intercept)'),
  b1 = c('logvol_t0'),
  b2 = c('logvol_t0_2', 'I(logvol_t0^2)'),
  b3 = c('logvol_t0_3', 'I(logvol_t0^3)'),
  bf = c('disturbance1', 'regex:^disturbance'))

# Flowering disturbance term map
lagged_size_term_map <- list(
  b0 = c("(Intercept)"),
  b1 = c("logvol_t0"),
  b2 = c("logvol_t0_2", "I(logvol_t0^2)"),
  b3 = c("logvol_t0_3", "I(logvol_t0^3)"),
  bf = c(
    "disturbance_prev1",
    "regex:^disturbance_prev"))

make_term_map <- function(prefix, map) {
  out <- map
  names(out) <- paste0(prefix, names(out))
  out
}

su_term_map <- make_term_map('surv_', size_term_map)
gr_term_map <- make_term_map('grow_', size_term_map)
fl_term_map  <- make_term_map("fl_",  lagged_size_term_map)
fln_term_map <- make_term_map("fln_", lagged_size_term_map)

  re_b0 = c('(Intercept)'),
  re_b1 = c('fs_t0_log'),
  re_bd = c('disturbance'),
  re_bf = c(
    'fs_t0_log:disturbance',
    'disturbance:fs_t0_log'))
```

## IPM helper functions
```{r}
inv_logit <- function(x) {
  plogis(x)
}

get_par <- function(pars, par_name, default = 0) {
  if (!is.null(pars[[par_name]])) {
    return(pars[[par_name]])
  }
  default
}

make_ipm_pars <- function(
    pars_mean,
    pars_year = NULL,
    pars_re_year_t1 = NULL,
    year = NULL,
    re_year_t1 = NULL) {
  pars <- pars_mean
  
  if (!is.null(year) && !is.null(pars_year)) {
    year <- as.character(year)
    year_hits <- grep(paste0('_', year, '$'), names(pars_year), value = TRUE)
    
    for (nm in year_hits) {
      base_nm <- sub(paste0('_', year, '$'), '', nm)
      pars[[base_nm]] <- pars_year[[nm]]
    }
  }
  
  if (is.null(re_year_t1) && !is.null(year)) {
    re_year_t1 <- as.numeric(as.character(year)) + 1
  }
  
  if (!is.null(re_year_t1) && !is.null(pars_re_year_t1)) {
    re_year_t1 <- as.character(re_year_t1)
    pars$re_b0 <- get_par(pars, 're_b0', 0) +
      get_par(
        pars_re_year_t1,
        paste0('re_u0_year_t1_', re_year_t1), 0)
    pars$re_b1 <- get_par(pars, 're_b1', 0) +
      get_par(
        pars_re_year_t1,
        paste0('re_u1_year_t1_', re_year_t1), 0)
  }
  
  pars
}

surv_lp <- function(x, pars, disturbance = 0) {
  get_par(pars, 'surv_b0', 0) +
    get_par(pars, 'surv_b1', 0) * x +
    get_par(pars, 'surv_b2', 0) * x^2 +
    get_par(pars, 'surv_b3', 0) * x^3 +
    get_par(pars, 'surv_bf', 0) * disturbance
}

sx <- function(x, pars, disturbance = 0) {
  inv_logit(surv_lp(x, pars, disturbance))
}

grow_mu <- function(x, pars, disturbance = 0) {
  get_par(pars, 'grow_b0', 0) +
    get_par(pars, 'grow_b1', 0) * x +
    get_par(pars, 'grow_b2', 0) * x^2 +
    get_par(pars, 'grow_b3', 0) * x^3 +
    get_par(pars, 'grow_bf', 0) * disturbance
}

grow_sd <- function(x, pars) {
  sqrt(pars$a * exp(pars$b * x))
}

gxy <- function(x, y, pars, disturbance = 0) {
  dnorm(
    y,
    mean = grow_mu(x, pars, disturbance),
    sd = grow_sd(x, pars))
}

# Flowering probability
fl_x <- function(x, pars, disturbance = 0) {
  eta <- get_par(pars, 'fl_b0', 0) +
    get_par(pars, 'fl_b1', 0) * x +
    get_par(pars, 'fl_b2', 0) * x^2 +
    get_par(pars, 'fl_b3', 0) * x^3 +
    get_par(pars, 'fl_bf', 0) * disturbance
  
  inv_logit(eta)
}


# Flowering-stem number conditional on flowering
fl_n_x <- function(x, pars, disturbance = 0) {
  eta <- get_par(pars, 'fln_b0', 0) +
    get_par(pars, 'fln_b1', 0) * x +
    get_par(pars, 'fln_b2', 0) * x^2 +
    get_par(pars, 'fln_b3', 0) * x^3 +
    get_par(pars, 'fln_bf', 0) * disturbance
  
  exp(eta)
}


# Expected flowering stems per individual
fs_x <- function(x, pars, disturbance = 0) {
  fl_x(x, pars, disturbance) * fl_n_x(x, pars, disturbance)
}


# Flowering-stem reference
get_fs_ref <- function(pars, disturbance = 0) {
  if (disturbance == 1) {
    get_par(pars, 'fs_t0_ref_1')
  } else {
    get_par(pars, 'fs_t0_ref_0')
  }
}


# Flowering-stem-to-recruit conversion
re_total_ref <- function(pars, disturbance = 0) {
  re_intercept <- get_par(pars, 're_b0', 0) +
    get_par(pars, 're_bd', 0) * disturbance
  
  re_slope <- get_par(pars, 're_b1', 0) +
    get_par(pars, 're_bf', 0) * disturbance
  
  fs_ref <- get_fs_ref(pars, disturbance)
  
  re_log <- re_intercept + re_slope * log1p(fs_ref)
  
  re_value <- expm1(
    re_log + 0.5 * get_par(pars, 're_sigma', 0)^2)
  
  pmax(re_value, 0)
}


rx <- function(x, pars, disturbance = 0) {
  fs_value <- fs_x(x, pars, disturbance)
  fs_ref <- get_fs_ref(pars, disturbance)
  re_ref <- re_total_ref(pars, disturbance)
  
  re_per_fs <- re_ref / pmax(fs_ref, .Machine$double.eps)
  
  fs_value * re_per_fs
}


# Recruit size distribution
re_y_dist <- function(y, pars, h = NULL) {
  dens <- dnorm(y, mean = pars$recr_sz, sd = pars$recr_sd)
  
  if (!is.null(h)) {
    dens <- dens / sum(dens * h)
  }
  
  dens
}


# Fertility matrix
fyx <- function(y, x, pars, h, disturbance = 0) {
  Pvec <- re_y_dist(y, pars, h = h)
  Rvec <- rx(x, pars, disturbance)
  
  outer(Pvec, Rvec) * h
}
```


## Kernel: historical size-structured
```{r}
kernel <- function(pars, disturbance = 0) {
  n <- pars$mat_siz
  L <- pars$L
  U <- pars$U
  h <- (U - L) / n
  b <- L + c(0:n) * h
  y <- 0.5 * (b[1:n] + b[2:(n + 1)])
  
  S <- sx(y, pars, disturbance = disturbance)
  
  G <- t(outer(
    y, y, Vectorize(function(x, y) {
      gxy(x, y, pars, disturbance = disturbance)
    }))) * h
  
  for (i in 1:n) {
    if (i <= n / 2) {
      G[1, i] <- G[1, i] + 1 - sum(G[, i])
    } else {
      G[n, i] <- G[n, i] + 1 - sum(G[, i])
    }
  }
  
  T <- sweep(G, 2, S, '*')
  
  F <- fyx(
    y = y,
    x = y,
    pars = pars,
    h = h,
    disturbance = disturbance)
  
  k_yx <- T + F
  
  Imat <- diag(n)
  Zmat <- matrix(0, n, n)
  
  K_hist <- rbind(
    cbind(T, F),
    cbind(Imat, Zmat))
  
  list(
    k_yx = k_yx,
    K_hist = K_hist,
    T = T,
    F = F,
    Imat = Imat,
    Zmat = Zmat,
    G = G,
    S = S,
    meshpts = y,
    h = h,
    L = L,
    U = U)
}

lambda_ipm <- function(pars, disturbance = 0) {
  K <- kernel(
    pars = pars,
    disturbance = disturbance)$K_hist
  
  Re(eigen(K, only.values = TRUE)$values[1])
}
```

```{r}
lambda_ipm(pars_mean, disturbance = 0)
lambda_ipm(pars_mean, disturbance = 1)
```

## Historical kernel diagnostics by year
```{r}
df_hist_kernel_check <- bind_rows(
  lapply(ipm_years, function(year_i) {
    pars_i <- make_ipm_pars(
      pars_mean = pars_all_mean,
      pars_year = pars_all_year,
      pars_re_year_t1 = pars_all_re_year_t1,
      year = year_i,
      re_year_t1 = year_i + 1)
    
    bind_rows(
      lapply(c(0, 1), function(disturbance_i) {
        kern_i <- kernel(
          pars = pars_i,
          disturbance = disturbance_i)
        
        n <- pars_i$mat_siz
        K <- kern_i$K_hist
        
        tibble(
          year = year_i,
          disturbance = disturbance_i,
          n_rows = nrow(K),
          n_cols = ncol(K),
          identity_block = isTRUE(all.equal(
            K[(n + 1):(2 * n), 1:n],
            diag(n))),
          zero_block = all(
            K[(n + 1):(2 * n), (n + 1):(2 * n)] == 0),
          any_nonfinite = any(!is.finite(K)))
      }))
  }))

df_hist_kernel_check
```


## Observed and projected population growth
Observed growth is calculated from quadrats represented in t - 1, t, and t + 1. Each quadrat is projected with its observed disturbance at year t.


### Quadrat-year disturbance lookup
```{r}
fire_lookup_quad <- df %>%
  group_by(site, quad, year) %>%
  summarise(
    disturbance_num = first(
      disturbance[!is.na(disturbance)],
      default = NA_real_),
    .groups = 'drop')
```

### Quadrat-year abundance
Counts include sized plants and recruits without a usable size measurement.
```{r}
df_counts_quad_year <- df %>%
  filter(
    !is.na(site),
    !is.na(quad),
    !is.na(year)) %>%
  group_by(
    site,
    quad,
    year) %>%
  summarise(
    n_sized = sum(
      is.finite(logvol_t0),
      na.rm = TRUE),
    n_unsized_recruits = sum(
      !is.finite(logvol_t0) & recruits == 1,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    n_ipm_state = n_sized + n_unsized_recruits,
    .groups = 'drop')
```

### Matched consecutive quadrat transitions
```{r}
df_obs_pgr_quad <- df_counts_quad_year %>%
  arrange(site, quad, year) %>%
  group_by(site, quad) %>%
  mutate(
    year_tm1 = lag(year),
    n_tm1 = lag(n_ipm_state),
    year_t1 = lead(year),
    n_t1 = lead(n_ipm_state),
    year_gap_prev = year - year_tm1,
    year_gap_next = year_t1 - year) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(
    year_gap_prev == 1,
    year_gap_next == 1,
    n_ipm_state > 0) %>%
  rename(n_t0 = n_ipm_state) %>%
  left_join(
    fire_lookup_quad,
    by = c('site', 'quad', 'year')) %>%
  filter(!is.na(disturbance_num)) %>%
  mutate(obs_pgr = n_t1 / n_t0)
```

### Initial quadrat size distribution
```{r}
make_initial_n_quad <- function(
    year0,
    site_i,
    quad_i,
    pars) {
  
  n <- pars$mat_siz
  L <- pars$L
  U <- pars$U
  h <- (U - L) / n
  
  breaks <- seq(
    L,
    U,
    length.out = n + 1)
  
  b <- L + c(0:n) * h
  
  y <- 0.5 *
    (b[1:n] + b[2:(n + 1)])
  
  df0 <- df %>%
    filter(
      year == year0,
      site == site_i,
      quad == quad_i)
  
  sizes <- df0 %>%
    filter(
      is.finite(logvol_t0)) %>%
    pull(logvol_t0)
  
  size_counts <- hist(
    pmin(
      pmax(sizes, L),
      U),
    breaks = breaks,
    plot = FALSE,
    include.lowest = TRUE)$counts
  
  n_density <- size_counts / h
  
  n_unsized_recruits <- df0 %>%
    summarise(
      n = sum(
        !is.finite(logvol_t0) &
          recruits == 1,
        na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    pull(n)
  
  if (n_unsized_recruits > 0) {
    n_density <- n_density +
      n_unsized_recruits *
      re_y_dist(
        y,
        pars,
        h = h)
  }
  
  n_density
}
```

### Project one quadrat-year
```{r}
project_one_quad_year <- function(
    yr,
    site_i,
    quad_i,
    disturbance_y) {
  
  pars_y <- make_ipm_pars(
    pars_mean = pars_all_mean,
    pars_year = pars_all_year,
    pars_re_year_t1 = pars_all_re_year_t1,
    year = yr,
    re_year_t1 = yr + 1)
  
  n_current <- make_initial_n_quad(
    year0 = yr,
    site_i = site_i,
    quad_i = quad_i,
    pars = pars_y)
  
  n_previous <- make_initial_n_quad(
    year0 = yr - 1,
    site_i = site_i,
    quad_i = quad_i,
    pars = pars_y)
  
  n_hist <- c(n_current, n_previous)
  
  K <- kernel(
    pars = pars_y,
    disturbance = disturbance_y)$K_hist
  
  n <- pars_y$mat_siz
  h <- (pars_y$U - pars_y$L) / n
  
  n_initial <- sum(n_current) * h
  
  if (n_initial <= 0) {
    return(
      data.frame(
        year = yr,
        site = site_i,
        quad = quad_i,
        disturbance_num = disturbance_y,
        n_obs_model = n_initial,
        n_proj_model = NA_real_,
        asym_lambda = NA_real_,
        proj_lambda = NA_real_))
  }
  
  n_proj_hist <- as.numeric(K %*% n_hist)
  n_next <- n_proj_hist[1:n]
  n_projected <- sum(n_next) * h
  
  data.frame(
    year = yr,
    site = site_i,
    quad = quad_i,
    disturbance_num = disturbance_y,
    n_obs_model = n_initial,
    n_proj_model = n_projected,
    asym_lambda = Re(eigen(K, only.values = TRUE)$values[1]),
    proj_lambda = n_projected / n_initial)
}
```


### Project all matched quadrat transitions
```{r}
df_proj_quad <- bind_rows(
  lapply(
    seq_len(nrow(df_obs_pgr_quad)),
    function(i) {
      
      project_one_quad_year(
        yr = df_obs_pgr_quad$year[i],
        site_i = df_obs_pgr_quad$site[i],
        quad_i = df_obs_pgr_quad$quad[i],
        disturbance_y = df_obs_pgr_quad$disturbance_num[i])
    }))
```


### Quadrat-level observed and modeled growth
```{r}
df_compare_quad <- df_obs_pgr_quad %>%
  left_join(
    df_proj_quad,
    by = c(
      'year',
      'site',
      'quad',
      'disturbance_num')) %>%
  mutate(
    error_asymptotic_vs_obs =
      asym_lambda - obs_pgr,
    error_projected_vs_obs =
      proj_lambda - obs_pgr)
```

### Site-year comparison from matched quadrats
```{r}
df_compare_site <- df_compare_quad %>%
  group_by(
    site,
    year) %>%
  summarise(
    asym_lambda = weighted.mean(
      asym_lambda,
      w = n_obs_model,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    n_t0 = sum(
      n_t0,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    n_t1 = sum(
      n_t1,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    n_obs_model = sum(
      n_obs_model,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    n_proj_model = sum(
      n_proj_model,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    n_quadrats = n(),
    n_burned_quadrats = sum(
      disturbance_num == 1,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    disturbance_num = as.numeric(
      any(
        disturbance_num == 1,
        na.rm = TRUE)),
    .groups = 'drop') %>%
  mutate(
    obs_pgr = n_t1 / n_t0,
    proj_lambda = n_proj_model / n_obs_model,
    error_asymptotic_vs_obs =
      asym_lambda - obs_pgr,
    error_projected_vs_obs =
      proj_lambda - obs_pgr)

df_compare_site %>%
  print(
    n = 100,
    width = Inf)
```

### Whole-population annual comparison
Annual totals contain only quadrats represented in t - 1, t, and t + 1.
```{r}
df_compare <- df_compare_quad %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  summarise(
    asym_lambda = weighted.mean(
      asym_lambda,
      w = n_obs_model,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    n_t0 = sum(
      n_t0,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    n_t1 = sum(
      n_t1,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    n_obs_model = sum(
      n_obs_model,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    n_proj_model = sum(
      n_proj_model,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    n_quadrats = n(),
    n_sites = n_distinct(site),
    n_burned_quadrats = sum(
      disturbance_num == 1,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    p_burned_quadrats = mean(
      disturbance_num == 1,
      na.rm = TRUE),
    disturbance = if_else(
      any(
        disturbance_num == 1,
        na.rm = TRUE),
      'Fire',
      'No fire'),
    .groups = 'drop') %>%
  mutate(
    obs_pgr = n_t1 / n_t0,
    proj_lambda = n_proj_model / n_obs_model,
    disturbance = factor(
      disturbance,
      levels = c(
        'No fire',
        'Fire')))

# Observed vs modeled plot
```

```{r}
    arithmetic_mean_proj_lambda = mean(proj_lambda, na.rm = TRUE),

    mean_error_projected_vs_obs = mean(
      proj_lambda - obs_pgr, na.rm = TRUE),
    percent_bias_asymptotic_vs_obs = 100 * sum(
      asym_lambda - obs_pgr, na.rm = TRUE) /
```
